input: Simulate a build pipeline: 1) Check that /src/main.c and /src/utils.c exist, 2) 'Compile' each .c file by copying it to /build/ with a .o extension and prepending '// compiled', 3) 'Link' by concatenating all .o files into /build/program with a '// linked' header, 4) 'Package' by creating a tar.gz of /build/ at /dist/release.tar.gz. Print status for each stage. If any stage fails, stop and report the error.

transcript.final_response:
The pipeline ran with no errors. `/src` already held `main.c` and `utils.c`. `/build` and `/dist` didn't exist, so the script created them.

1. **Check:** `/src/main.c` and `/src/utils.c` both exist.
2. **Compile:** I wrote `/build/main.o` and `/build/utils.o`, each with `// compiled` on the first line followed by the source. The loop compiled every `.c` file in `/src`, which here was just those two.
3. **Link:** I wrote `/build/program`, starting with `// linked` and followed by the contents of all the `.o` files.
4. **Package:** I created `/dist/release.tar.gz`. Listing it shows `build/`, `build/main.o`, `build/utils.o` and `build/program`.
tool_calls:
ls -la /src /dist 2>&1; echo ---
set -e
fail(){ echo "[FAIL] $1"; exit 1; }
echo "== Stage 1: Check sources =="
for f in /src/main.c /src/utils.c; do [ -f "$f" ] || fail "missing $f"; done
echo "[OK] sources found"
echo "== Stage 2: Compile =="
mkdir -p /build || fail "mkdir /build"
for f in /src/*.c; do
  o=/build/$(basename "${f%.c}").o
  { echo "// compiled"; cat "$f"; } > "$o" || fail "compile $f"
  echo "  $f -> $o"
done
echo "[OK] compiled"
echo "== Stage 3: Link =="
{ echo "// linked"; cat /build/*.o; } > /build/program || fail "link"
echo "[OK] linked -> /build/program"
echo "== Stage 4: Package =="
mkdir -p /dist || fail "mkdir /dist"
tar -czf /dist/release.tar.gz -C / build || fail "tar"
tar -tzf /dist/release.tar.gz || fail "verify tar"
echo "[OK] packaged -> /dist/release.tar.gz"
